items.readable_text:
Content:
The explicit formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence is given by

Content:
[MATH: a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d,]

Content:
where [MATH: a_1] is the first term and [MATH: d] is a common difference.

Content:
To illustrate how this works, suppose we want to find the [MATH: 20]th term of the following arithmetic sequence:
[MATH: {\color{blue}2}, \: 5, \: 8, \: 11, \: 14, \: \ldots]

Content:
The first term is [MATH: a_1={\color{blue}2},] and the common difference is

Content:
[MATH: d=5-2={\color{red}3}.]

Content:
So, we can write the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of the sequence as follows:

Content:
[MATH: a_{n}|= a_{1} + (n − 1)d; = 2 + (n − 1)(3); = 2 + 3n − 3; = 3n − 1]

Content:
To find the [MATH: 20]th term, we can use this formula with [MATH: n=20\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: a_{n}|= 3n − 1; a_{20}|= 3(20) − 1; = 60 − 1; = 59]

Content:
Therefore, the [MATH: 20]th term is [MATH: a_{20}=59.] Using the formula was much quicker than writing out all [MATH: 20] terms of the sequence!

sections.normalized_html: Find the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is [MATH: 3] and the common difference is [MATH: 2.]
sections.readable_text: Find the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is [MATH: 3] and the common difference is [MATH: 2.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence is

[MATH: a_n= a_{1}+(n-1)d.]

We are told that the first term is [MATH: a_1={\color{blue}3}] and the common difference is [MATH: d={\color{red}2}.] So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

[MATH: \eqalign{ a_n &= a_{1}+(n-1)d \[3pt] &= {\color{blue}3} + (n - 1)({\color{red}2}) \[3pt] &= 3 + 2n -2 \[3pt] & =2n+1 }]

Therefore the formula for the [MATH: n]th term is [MATH: a_n = 2n+1.]

sections.normalized_html: Find the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is [MATH: 0] and the second term is [MATH: -2.] Express your answer in function notation.
sections.readable_text: Find the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is [MATH: 0] and the second term is [MATH: -2.] Express your answer in function notation.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

[MATH: f(n)= f(1)+(n-1)d.]

We are given the first term [MATH: f(1)={\color{blue}0}.] Also, the common difference of the sequence can be found as [MATH: d=-2 - 0 = {\color{red}-2}.]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

[MATH: \eqalign{ f(n)&= f(1)+(n-1)d \[3pt] &= {\color{blue}0} + (n - 1)({\color{red}-2}) \[3pt] &= 0 - 2n + 2 \[3pt] &= 2 - 2n }]

Therefore, the formula for the [MATH: n]th term is [MATH: f(n) = 2 - 2n.]

sections.normalized_html: Find the [MATH: 50]th term of the following arithmetic sequence. [MATH: -5, \: -8, \: -11, \: \ldots]
sections.readable_text:
Find the [MATH: 50]th term of the following arithmetic sequence.
[MATH: -5, \: -8, \: -11, \: \ldots]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence is

[MATH: a_n= a_{1}+(n-1)d.]

First, we will write the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

[MATH: {\color{blue}-5}, \: -8, \: -11, \ldots,]

we see that the first term is [MATH: a_1={\color{blue}-5}] and the common difference is

[MATH: d=-8-(-5)={\color{red}-3}.]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

[MATH: \eqalign{ a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d \[3pt] &= {\color{blue}-5} + (n - 1)({\color{red}-3}) \[3pt] & =-5 -3n + 3 \[3pt] &=-3n-2 }]

Now, we can use our formula to find the [MATH: 50]th term. All we have to do is substitute [MATH: n=50\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ a_n &=-3n-2 \[7pt] a_{50} &= -3(50)-2 \[3pt] &= -150-2 \[3pt] &= -152 }]

Therefore, the [MATH: 50]th term of the sequence is [MATH: a_{50}=-152.]

sections.normalized_html: Find the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of the arithmetic sequence that has a [MATH: 7]th term equal [MATH: -34] and a common difference of [MATH: -5.]
sections.readable_text: Find the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of the arithmetic sequence that has a [MATH: 7]th term equal [MATH: -34] and a common difference of [MATH: -5.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, notice that [MATH: a_{7}=-34] is [MATH: 6] jumps after [MATH: a_1].

Hence, we can write [MATH: a_{7} = a_1 + 6d,] and solve for [MATH: a_1], as follows:

[MATH: a_{7}|= a_{1} + 6d; − 34|= a_{1} + 6(− 5); − 34|= a_{1} − 30; − 4|= a_{1}]

So, the formula for the [MATH: n]th term is:

[MATH: a_{n}|= a_{1} + (n − 1)d; = − 4 + (n − 1)(− 5); = − 4 − 5n + 5; = 1 − 5n]

Item 8 — Example: Finding a Particular Term of an Arithmetic Sequence

Example Prompt:
Find the [MATH: 50]th term of the following arithmetic sequence.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The formula for the [MATH: n]th term of an arithmetic sequence is

[MATH: a_n= a_{1}+(n-1)d.]

First, we will write the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

[MATH: {\color{blue}-5}, \: -8, \: -11, \ldots,]

we see that the first term is [MATH: a_1={\color{blue}-5}] and the common difference is

[MATH: d=-8-(-5)={\color{red}-3}.]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

[MATH: \eqalign{
a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d \[3pt]
&= {\color{blue}-5} + (n - 1)({\color{red}-3}) \[3pt]
& =-5 -3n + 3 \[3pt]
&=-3n-2
}]

Now, we can use our formula to find the [MATH: 50]th term. All we have to do is substitute [MATH: n=50\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{
a_n &=-3n-2 \[7pt]
a_{50} &= -3(50)-2 \[3pt]

}]

Therefore, the [MATH: 50]th term of the sequence is [MATH: a_{50}=-152.]
